newsitem.title: FRANCE: Former Riviera boss says innocent of sleaze.
newsitem.headline: Former Riviera boss says innocent of sleaze.

text.p: A former Riviera political boss who liked to be known as "the Godfather" on Friday dismissed court charges he took kickbacks and his lawyers denounced the sleaze trial as "political assassination".

The court in the Mediterranean port of Toulon said it would deliver a verdict on December 16 over allegations that Maurice Arreckx, 79, extorted 1.8 million francs ($350,000) in return for awarding a construction contract in the town in 1991.
Arreckx, the representative of the southern Var department to the French senate when arrested in August 1994, told reporters after the trial he was "totally innocent".
He said he was surprised by the public prosecutor's request that he go to jail for three years with a further two suspended. Arreckx has already spent 288 days in jail in pre-trial detention.

Lawyers for Arreckx, mayor of Toulon for 26 years until 1985, said the evidence against him was based on "rumours or slander" and denounced what they called "political terror" and "political assassination".

After a week-long trial, Arreckx said the best judge was "the popular court of ordinary people, who salute me, embrace me in the street. That court is favourable to me overall. I am confident in the...justice of my country."

The Var has been under the spotlight since 1993 when local parliamentarian Yann Piat, like Arreckx a member of the centrist Union for French Democracy, was killed after she threatened to reveal "Mafia-like" activities in the region.
In a letter made public after her death, Piat told friends that if she were killed, Arreckx should be among the suspects.

Another top southern politician, Cannes mayor Michel Mouillot, is in detention on suspicion of extorting cash from a British casino. And mayors of Nice, Lyon and Grenoble have all been embroiled in political scandals.
